scientific_question: Are there independently documented, georeferenced and dated butterfly larval feeding records in regions where a known host plant is classified as introduced? This is needed to connect potential larval-resource reconstructions to realized biological use.
source: Global Biotic Interactions observation-level interaction.csv includeObservations=true; no HOSTS-only assertion can count as independent

sample_design.butterfly_families: two from each of five families plus one from Riodinidae; selected for probe only, NOT representative
sample_design.pagination: Two 512-row pages per species; never interpret missing records as zero if capped

stages.A: all returned interactions with complete source and target taxa and plausible plant targets
stages.B: geocoordinates and event year (1800-2025), life stage recorded or missing distinctly
stages.C: strict evidence: butterfly source life stage explicitly larva/caterpillar, herbivorous ingestion relationship, plant taxon, year, coordinates, and identified non-HOSTS study provenance
stages.D: join strict evidence to exact frozen HOSTS × WCVP (introduced plant in WGSRPD3, focal butterfly has no native known-host resource in that region)

filtering.invalid: lat/lon missing/out of bounds/0,0; non-larval or unknown stage never assumed larval; flower visitation not larval use
filtering.not_independent: HOSTS-like source citations flagged and excluded from strict evidence; ambiguous sources are unknown not independent
filtering.aliases: no synonym guessing in strict species-level join
filtering.sampling: GloBI REST snapshots can change; archive raw pages or their checksums, retrieval date and source citations

pass: At least 10 independently sourced georeferenced dated larval host-use records in introduced-host regions, spanning >=3 butterfly species and >=3 WGSRPD3 regions; move to source verification, not hypothesis testing
fail: Do not invent a realized host-use endpoint from a static HOSTS link. If thin, retain structural finding but do not write a realized butterfly ecology article from it.
prior_ecological_results: family×botanical-family conditional structural excess ~0.0105 Jaccard p=0.030; full-history butterfly short-window hindcast not supported
